title: Pedagogical AI conversational agents in higher education: a conceptual framework and survey of the state of the art
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the rapidly expanding use of pedagogical AI conversational agents in higher education and the need for a structured account of their current state of the art. The authors ask how these agents are being used, what pedagogical and technological functions they serve, and which areas remain underexplored. Rather than testing a single intervention, the paper surveys and synthesizes prior work to build a conceptual framework for categorising conversational agents in higher education.

The study reviews 92 papers published between 2014 and 2022, identified through searches of ACM Digital Library, ScienceDirect, ProQuest, IEEE Xplore, Scopus, and Web of Science. Using thematic template analysis, the authors organise agents along two main dimensions: pedagogical applications and technological functions. Pedagogical uses are grouped into instructional, pastoral, and cognitive purposes, with finer-grained intents such as mentoring and coaching, motivation, communication, assessment, reflective/metacognitive support, FAQ/knowledge-base support, and simulation/experience. Technological functions are organised by embodiment, functional type, and implementation features such as NLP, machine learning, external data sources, and social/IM platform integration.

The review covers higher education contexts that include both face-to-face and distance/online delivery, and the examples span students in undergraduate and graduate-level settings. The paper concludes that conversational agents are most commonly used for instructional and pastoral purposes, while cognitive and assessment-oriented uses are less explored. The authors argue that future research should place greater emphasis on reflective practice, personalisation, richer interaction, and more advanced pedagogical applications, including better support for assessment and administration.

identified_tools.name: CAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Conversational AI / pedagogical conversational agents used for instructional, pastoral, and cognitive educational interactions, including chatbots, virtual agents, voice bots, and virtual humans.
identified_tools.use_case: Systematic review and conceptual framework of pedagogical AI conversational agents used in higher education from 2014-2022.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a review/conceptual framework paper rather than a primary evaluation study. It synthesizes prior literature and does not report an empirical trial of a single tool with effect estimates.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper has conceptual and field-mapping value, but it does not report measured learning or teacher outcomes for a specific intervention. Any impact is therefore indirect and not quantifiable from this paper.
